hints: Focus on the balanced equation for complete combustion of ethane, since gas volumes react in the same ratio as moles.
Notice that 10 cm3 of ethane needs 35 cm3 of oxygen, so oxygen is in excess and 10 cm3 will be left over.
Remember the temperature is 200 C, so water is steam and counts as gas, then add leftover oxygen to both gaseous products to get the final total.
walkthrough:
**Write the balanced equation for complete combustion**

Think of complete combustion as ethane plus oxygen making only carbon dioxide and water. Balancing gives the volume ratio.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 + 3.5\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So 1 volume of ethane reacts with 3.5 volumes of oxygen to make 2 volumes of carbon dioxide and 3 volumes of water.

**Find how much oxygen is used and left over**

We start with 10 cm3 ethane, so just scale the ratio up by 10. This tells us if oxygen limits the reaction.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$V(\text{O}_2 \text{ needed}) = 10 \times 3.5 = 35 \text{ cm}^3$$
$$V(\text{O}_2 \text{ leftover}) = 45 - 35 = 10 \text{ cm}^3$$
Oxygen is in excess, ethane is fully used up.

**Add up all gases present at the end**

At 200 C water is a gas, so do not ignore it. Both products stay in the gas mixture along with the leftover oxygen.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$V(\text{CO}_2) = 10 \times 2 = 20 \text{ cm}^3$$
$$V(\text{H}_2\text{O}) = 10 \times 3 = 30 \text{ cm}^3$$
$$V(\text{total}) = 20 + 30 + 10 = 60 \text{ cm}^3$$

options.A: Incorrect. 30 cm3 is what you get if you wrongly treat water as a liquid and exclude it: 20 cm3 CO2 + 10 cm3 leftover O2 = 30 cm3. At 200 C, well above 100 C, water is steam and must be counted as 30 cm3 of gas.
options.B: Incorrect. 50 cm3 is the volume of the products only: 20 cm3 CO2 + 30 cm3 H2O. This forgets the 10 cm3 of excess oxygen that did not react but is still present as gas.
options.C: Incorrect. 55 cm3 is simply the starting total, 10 + 45, with no allowance for the mole change in the reaction. Gas volumes change according to the balanced equation, they are not conserved.
options.D: Correct. 10 cm3 ethane uses 35 cm3 O2, leaving 10 cm3 O2. It forms 20 cm3 CO2 and 30 cm3 gaseous H2O at 200 C. Total gas = 20 + 30 + 10 = 60 cm3.
